title.official: Time limit for application to disallow amendment to pleading

division.heading: Request for Particulars, Amendments to Pleadings and Close of Pleadings

operative_text.controlling:
3.64(1)  On application, the Court may disallow an amendment to
a pleading or a part of it.
(2)  The application must be filed within 10 days after service on
the applicant of the amended pleading.

BOOK_A.title: Time Limit for Application to Disallow Amendment to Pleading
BOOK_A.commentary:
Rule 3.64 lets the court disallow unilateral pleadings, presumably when they violate the Rules. But there is a short time limit for applying to disallow;that Rule and R.1.5(2) and (3) show that a

belated application to disallow a R.3.64 amendment may well fail. *Permission of Court to Amendment Before or After Close of Pleadings*3*
BOOK_A.footnotes_note: not split out: this extraction prints footnotes as unmarked text inside the page (see commentary); nothing was dropped
BOOK_A.operative_text_note: same wording as official 3.64(1)-(2) (read by eye) except: the title in title case ('Time Limit for Application to Disallow Amendment to Pleading', printed before the rule number); missing spaces; '*' line marks; the footnote marker '1' after the last word. No amendment bracket; the official text lists only 'AR 124/2010' (no amending regulation). No substantive difference. The history footnote 1 ('Quite similar to previous 1968 R.131. It came from 1944 C.R.193. Cf. Judic.Ord. r.181, and 1883 O.28 r.4.') matching the marker is printed at p.3-137 line 3867 in the built 3.63 record.
BOOK_A.commentary_review_flag: Read in full, p.3-137 (lines 3871-3874): rule text, Defined Terms 'Court, file, pleading' (the Appendix defines each), Related Provisions '3.68 (deficient pleadings)' and a two-sentence note; no Information Note. The built record: defined_terms, related_provisions and the note in the commentary field (ending with the heading of 3.65 'Permission of Court to Amendment Before or After Close of Pleadings' and the marker '3'); nothing dropped. (1) Related Provisions: '3.68 (deficient pleadings)' - official 3.68 is 'Court options to deal with significant deficiencies'. (2) Note read against the official text: 'Rule 3.64 lets the court disallow unilateral pleadings, presumably when they violate the Rules' - 3.64(1) says 'the Court may disallow an amendment to a pleading or a part of it' and states no ground; 'there is a short time limit for applying to disallow; that Rule and R.1.5(2) and (3) show that a belated application to disallow a R.3.64 amendment may well fail' - 3.64(2) sets 10 days after service on the applicant of the amended pleading; official 1.5(2) (an application under 1.5 must be filed within a reasonable time after the applicant becomes aware) and 1.5(3) (no application by a party who has taken a further step in the action knowing of the prejudice) were read and agree with the note's statement that a belated application may fail. (3) History: fn 1 (1968 R.131; 1944 C.R.193; Judic.Ord. r.181; 1883 O.28 r.4) is this rule's (marker '1' after (2)); it is printed in the 3.63 record. (4) Book A prints no other note; Book B and Book C print no commentary. Pointers to 3.64: Book A p.3-161 (line 4765) '3.64 (striking amendments)' in the related provisions of a rule not identified here; no other citation found (cross-reference helper: official, all Book A, B, C files).
